source_verification_receipts.version: Annals of Statistics 32(5), 2004 version of record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies Gaussian nonparametric confidence intervals for linear functionals; between-class moduli control expected length and yield sharp lower bounds.
The paper derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds for linear regression functionals over convex classes under normal errors with known variance.
The paper develops design-based minimax risk under arbitrary neighborhood interference and gives upper/lower minimax-rate bounds through conflict-graph connectivity for direct and global effects.
The paper gives nonasymptotic treatment-effect intervals for randomized experiments with effective sample sizes matching asymptotic counterparts and information-theoretic unimprovability claims.
The paper constructs randomized/fuzzy confidence intervals and discusses an expected-length lower bound with a Bernoulli observation example.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add an explicit hard-subexperiment definition mapping V to bounded block-homogeneous potential outcomes, retaining all assignment ancillaries, and a measurable Gamma-to-Lambda reduction that preserves coverage and expected length.

Make the software artifact mathematical: add a versioned package-label function as an input to Phi, state its domain/codomain, and distinguish recomputed reference labels from externally returned labels.
After the embedding is repaired, sharpen the global OEQ with a finite-dimensional least-favorable family or a proved two-block lower corollary before pursuing the full water-filling equivalence.

recommended_next_step: Revise the two missing mathematical interfaces, then advance this field-level unequal-clique confidence-frontier angle to Stage 0.
